title: Top Payroll Software for Small Business in 2026
summary: Stop re-keying hours. Compare payroll software for small business on verified pricing, tax filing, time tracking, and support, then pick the right fit.
body_markdown:
Your team clocks out on Friday afternoon, payroll is due Monday, and the hours in your spreadsheet don’t match the time clock. You re-check the numbers, find a missed break, and start wondering what else slipped through. That gap between tracked hours and paychecks is where most small business payroll errors begin.


[Payroll software for small business](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-payroll-software-for-small-business) closes that gap by calculating wages, withholding taxes, paying your team by direct deposit and, on the right plan, filing the taxes for you. The differences show up in the details. Some tools include tax filing in the base price and others don’t. Hours reach payroll in different ways, extra states cost different amounts, and support answers at different speeds.


This guide compares seven payroll tools for businesses with fewer than 50 employees. We checked each tool’s pricing and features, read the patterns across Capterra, G2 and Reddit reviews, and noted where every tool falls short. Hourly teams, mixed salaried and hourly teams, and one-person payrolls each point to a different pick, so start with the quick list below.

## **The Top Payroll Software for Small Business, Reviewed**


Each entry follows the same order: a short assessment, who it fits, ratings, features, pricing, what users say, and our take. Ratings and review counts were checked on November 10, 2026.


### **Gusto**


Gusto is full-service payroll with benefits administration, built for small businesses that pay both salaried and hourly employees. It handles tax filing and direct deposit on every plan and adds HR tools as you move up. Teams that need time tracking or several states should plan on the Plus plan.


**Best for:** mixed salaried and hourly teams that want benefits in the same system.


**Rating:** G2 4.6 (13,963 reviews) · Capterra 4.6 (4,233 reviews).


**Key features:**


- Automatic federal and state tax filing.
- Unlimited payroll runs.
- Benefits administration (benefit products and costs vary).
- Contractor payments with 1099s.


**Pricing:** Simple starts at $49 a month plus $6 per person, and Plus starts at $80 plus $12 per person and adds time tracking, scheduling and multi-state payroll. There is no free tier.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/131882/Gusto/reviews/) and[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/gusto) reviewers describe Gusto as easy to learn, with solid automation and employee self-service.


**What users criticize:** reviewers report that support gets harder to reach on urgent or unusual issues, such as tax corrections, and that reporting is limited. Reddit threads include individual accounts of tax filing and data conversion problems. They show the kinds of issues owners raise, not how often they happen.


**Our take:** Gusto earns its reputation with mixed teams. The per-person cost climbs with headcount, Simple covers one state, and time tracking requires Plus, so hourly teams should price the full setup before choosing.


### **ADP RUN**


ADP RUN is payroll and HR for small businesses of one to 49 employees that expect to grow. It covers full-service payroll and multi-state tax filing, and it scales within the small business range. Pricing is quote-based, which makes early cost comparisons harder.


**Best for:** growing businesses that want payroll and HR tools with room to scale.


**Rating:** G2 4.7 (6,771 reviews) · Capterra 4.6.


**Key features:**


- Full-service payroll with tax filing.
- Multi-state payroll support, with state fees depending on the package.
- Real-person support from ADP’s payroll team.


**Pricing:** quote-based. You need to contact ADP for a price.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/185859/RUN/reviews/) reviewers praise the payroll processing, the time it saves and helpful support representatives.


**What users criticize:** some reviewers find navigation hard and the interface more corporate than small business tools. Certain tasks need a call to support or an added service instead of self-service.


**Our take:** RUN suits owners who want depth and expect to add employees and states. A five-person shop running simple hourly payroll will likely find the quote process and cost harder to justify.

If you don’t already use QuickBooks, other tools offer comparable payroll without an accounting subscription.

### **OnPay**


OnPay sells one full-service payroll plan at a flat monthly price, with multi-state tax filing and unlimited pay runs included. Setup and data migration are free, and HR and time tracking come in paid bundles. It works well for payroll-first businesses, though the base plan relies on integrations for time tracking.


**Best for:** businesses that want flat-rate payroll, including across several states.


**Rating:** G2 4.8 (422 reviews) · Capterra 4.8 (471 reviews).


**Key features:**


- Multi-state payroll included in the base price.
- Unlimited pay runs.
- Free setup and data migration.
- Tax filing guarantee.


**Pricing:** $49 a month plus $6 per worker, with the first month free as a current offer. Time Tracking adds $15 a month plus $4 per worker, and HR adds $15 plus $2 per worker. Bundles that include both start at a discounted $70 a month plus $10 per worker.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/167109/OnPay/reviews/) and[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/onpay-inc) reviewers highlight easy setup, helpful onboarding support and straightforward pricing.


**What users criticize:** reviewers note that the base plan has no built-in time tracking or scheduling, and some report slow W-2 corrections and want more payroll automation.


**Our take:** OnPay is a clean choice when payroll is the only job. On the base plan, hourly teams will need a separate time clock and an export step, which is the hand-off where errors tend to start.


### **Patriot**


Patriot offers the lowest starting price in this guide. Its Basic plan runs payroll but leaves tax filing to you, while Full Service files federal, state and local taxes. Direct deposit is free, and US-based support is included.


**Best for:** small businesses that want the lowest entry cost and simple payroll.


**Rating:** G2 4.8 (630 reviews) · Capterra 4.8 (3,969 reviews).


**Key features:**


- Unlimited payroll runs and free direct deposit.
- Full Service files federal, state and local payroll taxes and guarantees filing reliability.
- Free setup help.
- Time and attendance as an add-on.


**Pricing:** Basic is $17 a month plus $4 per worker. Full Service is $37 a month plus $5 per worker, with $12 a month for each added state. Time tracking adds $6 a month plus $2 per employee. There is no free tier, though new accounts get a 30-day trial.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/116050/Patriot-Software/reviews/) and[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/patriot-software/reviews) reviewers praise the price and the support.


**What users criticize:** some reviewers call the interface dated, and bonuses and PTO accruals can take manual steps. Direct deposit lead times also draw complaints. Patriot offers four-day standard and two-day expedited deposit for qualifying customers.


**Our take:** Patriot is the right answer when price leads and you can accept a slower deposit schedule. Basic leaves tax filing to you, and once you add Full Service and time tracking the total approaches Gusto and OnPay.


### **Square Payroll**


Square Payroll is built for businesses that already run Square point of sale. When you use Square’s point of sale and timekeeping, timecards and tips can flow into payroll, which removes manual transfer. Outside the Square ecosystem, the benefits shrink quickly.


**Best for:** Square POS users who want payroll in the same account.


**Rating:** G2 4.2 (31 reviews) · Capterra 4.7 (622 reviews).


**Key features:**


- Timecards and tips imported from Square.
- Unlimited pay runs.
- Employee access to pay stubs and hours.


**Pricing:** $35 a month plus $6 per person for employees and contractors.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/170266/Square-Payroll/reviews/) reviewers who already use Square describe the integration as easy, with tips added to paychecks automatically.


**What users criticize:** some reviewers report confusing onboarding and permissions, direct deposit problems, and tax filing errors that were hard to resolve. Reporting is also limited.


**Our take:** the G2 score rests on only 31 reviews, so treat it as a thin sample. If you already use Square and don’t need benefits administration, it is the easiest path. Otherwise the reports of filing errors make it harder to recommend.


### **Rippling**


Rippling combines payroll with HR, benefits and IT in one system. That breadth helps companies managing several entities or remote employees, but it adds setup time and cost. Smaller teams often use only a fraction of it.


**Best for:** teams that want payroll, HR and IT managed together.


**Rating:** G2 4.7 (15,123 reviews) · Capterra 4.8. These scores cover Rippling’s full HR system, not payroll alone.


**Key features:**


- Payroll connected to HR, benefits and device management.
- Automated workflows and customizable reports.
- Centralized employee data.


**Pricing:** custom quote, with payroll, HR and IT modules priced separately.


**What users like:**[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/172127/Rippling/reviews/) and[G2](https://www.g2.com/sellers/rippling) reviewers value having HR information, benefits and payroll in one place.


**What users criticize:** reviewers report add-on costs that make budgeting difficult, some support delays and limited flexibility on contracts and renewals. Some multi-location reviewers advise checking multi-location payroll before buying.


**Our take:** Rippling may fit a larger business with several locations or remote employees. For a five-person retail store, the cost and setup are hard to justify.

## **How to Choose Payroll Software for Small Business**


Six questions narrow the field quickly:


- **Is tax filing in the base price?** Federal, state and local filing and deposits should happen automatically. The IRS assigns monthly or semiweekly deposit schedules based on your prior tax liability, as explained in[IRS Publication 15](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) .
- **How long does direct deposit take?** Ask for the timeline in writing. Patriot, for example, offers four-day standard and two-day expedited deposit, so confirm lead times against your pay date.
- **How do hours reach payroll?** Re-keying hours is a common source of errors. A tool that connects the[time clock](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-employee-time-clock-app) to payroll removes that step.
- **Does it handle tips and overtime?** Starting with 2026 W-2s, qualifying tips and overtime must be reported separately.
- **What does the full price look like?** Add per-state fees, time tracking and HR add-ons to the base price.
- **Who answers when something breaks?** See the support section above.


### **Payroll Software for Hourly vs. Salaried Teams**


Salaried payroll is predictable, so the risk sits mostly at year-end. Hourly payroll changes every pay period because of overtime, shift differentials, multiple wage rates and tips. Choose a tool that connects time tracking and payroll so hours move from the clock to the paycheck without re-entry.


One owner described the pattern in an[r/smallbusiness thread](https://www.reddit.com/r/smallbusiness/comments/1pviibf/whats_the_best_payroll_software_for_small/) : payroll and time tracking ran in separate systems. Year-end became a scramble to pull reports from several places.


If you track hours in Homebase, you can send them to payroll without re-entering anything.


### **Payroll Software for One Employee**


A one-person payroll still needs tax filing, direct deposit and a W-2. With one worker paid, the monthly minimum among the plans priced here is $21 for Patriot Basic and $42 for Patriot Full Service. OnPay and Gusto Simple start at $55. Remember that Patriot Basic leaves tax filing to you.

## **Why Payroll Tax Penalties Cost More Than You Think**


Most payroll errors begin with a manual hand-off from the time clock to a spreadsheet to a paycheck. Penalties can apply even when an error is unintentional, though relief may be available for reasonable cause.


The IRS charges a failure-to-deposit penalty that rises with the delay:


- **One to five days late:** 2%.
- **Six to 15 days late:** 5%.
- **More than 15 days late:** 10%.


The rates do not stack. A 15% rate applies when a deposit is still unpaid more than 10 days after the first IRS notice or notice-and-demand for immediate payment. A $15,000 deposit made 16 days late would generally fall under the 10% tier and draw a $1,500 penalty, before interest. The IRS may reduce or remove some penalties when reasonable cause applies.


## **New in 2026: Tip and Overtime Reporting on Form W-2**


The One Big Beautiful Bill Act created deductions for qualified tips and[qualified overtime](https://www.joinhomebase.com/small-business-questions/how-does-no-tax-on-overtime-work) for tax years 2025 through 2028. Employees claim eligible deductions on their own returns, and Social Security and Medicare taxes still apply. Not all tips or overtime qualify, so employers report the amounts and the return determines eligibility. Employers report the amounts on the 2026 Form W-2, filed in early 2027, according to the[IRS General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/iw2w3) .


- **Box 12, code TP:** total cash tips reported to the employer.
- **Box 12, code TT:** total qualified overtime compensation. Only the premium portion counts, so in a time-and-a-half week you report the extra half.
- **Box 14b:** Treasury Tipped Occupation Codes, up to two based on the occupations where tips were received, reported along with code TP. Use 000 for a nonqualifying occupation.


The form also adds code TA for employer contributions to Trump accounts. Employers must file 2026 Forms W-2 and furnish employee copies by February 1, 2027. Ask any payroll provider you’re considering how it captures these fields before year-end.


## **How to Switch Payroll Software for Small Business**


Switching is straightforward when you plan it. Follow these steps:


1. Pull year-to-date wage and tax reports from your current provider before you cancel.
2. Gather W-4s, direct deposit details and current wage rates for every employee.
3. Choose a switch date. January 1 is cleanest if you can plan around year-end, and a mid-year switch needs a careful year-to-date transfer to avoid gaps in quarterly filings.
4. Set up the new provider and run a test payroll before your first live pay run.
5. Confirm tax registration in every state where you have employees.
6. Cancel the old provider only after the first payroll on the new system processes successfully and you have your year-to-date filings and final forms.


Ask each provider about setup help. Patriot enters employee data and year-to-date payroll for free, OnPay includes free setup and data migration, and Homebase[migrates your existing pay and tax data](https://www.joinhomebase.com/switch-payroll) . Riley McGuire, Director of HR at Student Agencies, says the team saved about $10,000 after deciding to[switch payroll providers](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-switch-payroll-providers) from ADP to Homebase. Lee Hartley, Director of Operations at Active Education, says payroll takes a couple of hours every two weeks.


## **Frequently Asked Questions About Payroll Software for Small Business**


### **What Is the Best Payroll Software for a Small Business?**


The[best choice](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/best-payroll-software-for-small-business) depends on your team. Hourly teams do best with payroll connected to time tracking. Mixed salaried and hourly teams with benefits needs often pick Gusto. Businesses already on QuickBooks can stay in that system. Compare tax filing coverage, per-state fees and support hours before you decide.


### **What’s the Best Payroll Software for a Multi-State Small Business?**


The best payroll software for a multi-state small business withholds and files taxes by each employee’s work state and keeps every filing in one place. OnPay includes multi-state filing in its base price, Gusto requires the Plus plan, and Homebase Payroll files by work state with reciprocity support for businesses under a single FEIN.


### **What Is the Best Free Payroll Software for Small Business?**


None of the tools ranked here is free forever, because tax filing and compliance carry ongoing costs. Free-only tools usually leave tax filing to you. Patriot offers a 30-day trial and OnPay a free first month, and our guide to[free payroll software](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/free-payroll-software-for-small-business) covers the no-cost options.


### **Can I Do My Own Payroll for My Small Business?**


Yes, but it takes more than most owners expect. You calculate gross pay and[withhold federal and state taxes](https://www.joinhomebase.com/blog/how-to-do-payroll-for-small-business) . You also follow monthly or semiweekly deposit schedules, file quarterly Form 941 and annual Form 940 as applicable, and issue W-2s by February 1, 2027. For one or two employees it is manageable, though the compliance risk often outweighs the savings.


### **Can I Just Use QuickBooks for Payroll?**


Yes, if you already run QuickBooks Online and want payroll in the same place. Payroll entries sync to your books, and tax filing is automated. Check current plan names and per-state fees first, and plan to bring in hours from a time clock or timesheet.


### **How Do I Do Payroll for My LLC?**


If your LLC has employees, you run payroll like any other employer. Get an EIN if you don’t have one, collect W-4s, withhold and deposit payroll taxes, and file Forms 941 and W-2. How you pay yourself depends on how the LLC is taxed, so ask a tax professional whether you take owner draws or wages.


### **What Payroll Software Has the Best Customer Support for Small Business?**


Support quality depends on hours, channels and who gets access. Homebase Payroll includes live chat and phone support from 7am to 7pm CT, Monday through Sunday, excluding holidays, plus a payroll expert for setup. Patriot offers weekday phone, email and chat until 7pm ET, and OnPay extends weekday hours to 8pm. Compare hours in your time zone.


### **What Payroll Software Works Best for Hourly Employees?**


Look for an app that handles variable hours, overtime, tip tracking and multiple wage rates, plus the 2026 W-2 codes for tips and overtime. Tools that connect time tracking to payroll remove re-entry, which is where errors start. Gusto includes time tracking in Plus, Patriot sells it as an add-on, and OnPay relies on integrations on its base plan.

Then check what the base price covers, since tax filing, extra states and time tracking are where costs add up.
